title: fix(lint): a context pack may name a system column the platform injects
body:
Fixes #37415

Clause-②: no (ADR-0160 D3: "A name the published definition lacks is an author defect"; an injected column is in the published definition, so the warning on it was the defect)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 写资料包的作者：在资料包里写平台自动加的字段（负责人、创建时间等），保存和校验时不再误报「字段不存在」；平台没加的字段照旧提醒。
- 属于「AI 资料包」专题的跟进，替写资料包的作者解决误报。
- 出错只会多报或少报一条提醒，资料包照常保存和读取；可以直接撤回。
- 无。

## What changes

Measured first, on one real kernel (the `/mcp` door, the real protocol, `SqlDriver`, `sys_user` registered as the platform registers it): on an object that declares neither `owner_id` nor `created_at`, the served object listing carries both (plus `organization_id`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `owning_business_unit_id`, `queue`), and `get_record_context` answers `owner_id` and `created_at` in the root's `fields` and in a related list's `fields` (`owner_id` as a lookup entry, its value marked `notVisible` because the harness caller cannot open the `sys_user` row, as for any lookup whose target row it cannot read), filters the list by a `where` on `owner_id` (one of two rows came back, the caller's) and orders it by `created_at`. On an `ownership: 'org'` object the listing carries no `owner_id` and the tool leaves it out. So the runtime carries injected columns, and the warning was false.

- `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts`: `fieldMapOf` now returns the effective map, the declared fields plus `injectedColumnDefsFor(object)` (this package's one indirection over the spec's `injectedSystemColumnDefs`, the tables `applySystemFields` and the served read's `applyInjectedSystemColumns` spread), a declared field winning. Every place the rule reads a field map reads it: root `fields`, `body.field`, related `fields`, `where`, `orderBy`, and the related link. The `orderBy` sortability projection now reads the same effective map instead of the declared fields.
- Consequences, each matching the runtime: a `body.field` naming an injected column is judged by its type (`ai-context-body-not-long-text`, as the executor reads the served definition); on a related list whose root is a `sys_*` object, the child's injected references to it (`owner_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by` to `sys_user`) count as links, as `resolveRelatedLink` counts them over the published definition, so a child with one declared reference and no `field` is reported as having several. No non-`sys_*` root is affected: every injected reference points at a `sys_*` object.
- A column the platform does not inject on that object is still reported: `owner_id` under `ownership: 'org'` / `'none'`, every system column under `systemFields: false`.
- `.changeset/37415-ai-context-injected-columns.md`: `@objectstack/lint` patch.

### Read first (by risk)

1. `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts`, the `fieldMapOf` hunk: the merge direction (declared wins) and the sortability line.
2. `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.test.ts`, the four new cases, especially the `sys_*` root link case.
3. `packages/services/service-record-context/src/__tests__/injected-system-columns.test.ts`: the executor half over a door serving the registry-injected shape.

### Two-minute verification

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/validate-ai-context.test.ts` shows 22 passed, including "an injected system column the object does not declare is no unknown field (owner_id, created_at)".

## Tests

- `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.test.ts`: `owner_id`, `created_at`, `created_by` in root `fields`, related `fields`, `where`, `orderBy` on objects that do not declare them: no finding. `ownership: 'org'` keeps `owner_id` unknown in all four places; `systemFields: false` keeps `created_at` unknown. `body.field: 'created_at'` is `ai-context-body-not-long-text`. `sys_*` root: injected references count as links.
- `packages/services/service-record-context/src/__tests__/injected-system-columns.test.ts` (new, read-only use of the service): over the fake door serving `injectedSystemColumnDefs` merged under the declared fields, the executor answers `owner_id` (with the `sys_user` display) and `created_at` in root and related fields, filters by `where: { owner_id }` and orders by `created_at desc`; the same pack over a door serving declared fields only leaves every such name and the list out, silently.

## Acceptance notes

- Acceptance bullet 1 (a test pins the lint verdict for `owner_id` on an object that does not declare it, matching the measured runtime answer): the first new lint case; the measured runtime answer is quoted in a comment above it and in the service test's header.
- Corroboration: the real-kernel harness on sibling PR #37412 shows the executor and both MCP doors read a related list ordered by `created_at` on an object that does not declare it, while the rule warned `ai-context-field-unknown`: the same runtime answer for `created_at` in `orderBy`, measured independently. `owner_id` was measured here.
- Measurement method: the real-kernel reading was a scratch copy of the real-protocol harness in `packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts`, run once and deleted, never committed (`packages/runtime/**` is fenced for this card). The committed pin of the executor half is the new service test over the fake door.
- Without `sys_user` registered (a composition the platform never ships), naming `owner_id` refuses the whole call `PERMISSION_DENIED` ("reads an object you cannot read"): `owner_id` is a lookup to `sys_user`, and an unreadable lookup target refuses the call, as for any lookup. Measured, noted, not filed.
- The `os explain` text for `ai-context-field-unknown` (`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`) still says "a name the object does not define"; it is outside this card's file surface and stays correct in substance (an injected column is defined on the object). Noted, not changed.
- An ADR-0015 `external` object carries injected columns with no storage behind them; this rule now lets a pack name one (the published definition carries it, so the executor plans it), and the read degrades at query time. The provenance warning other rules give (`unprovisionedInjectedColumnsFor`) is not wired into this rule. Filed as #37432 (an own rule id and an `os explain` entry), which also carries folding `injected-system-columns.test.ts` into `record-context-tools.test.ts` once #37361 lands.
- The new service test is a new file, as the dispatch order and the claim's file surface direct; the shared executor test file is owned by an in-flight sibling card.

## Verification

<details><summary>Real-kernel measurement (scratch, deleted)</summary>

```text
MEASURE served-listing rcm_policy fields: organization_id,created_at,created_by,updated_at,updated_by,owner_id,owning_business_unit_id,queue,title
MEASURE served-listing rcm_orgdoc fields: organization_id,created_at,created_by,updated_at,updated_by,title
rcm_brief (fields title, owner_id, created_at; related fields version, owner_id; where owner_id; orderBy created_at desc), sys_user registered:
  fields: title "Fire cover", owner_id (label Owner, notVisible: the sys_user row is not readable to this harness's caller), created_at "2026-11-26T03:16:17.088Z"
  related rcm_revision rows: r1 only (v1, owner_id) -- r2 (owner usr_other) filtered out by the where on owner_id
rcm_c (related fields version, created_at; where owner_id usr_member; orderBy created_at desc): rows r1 only (v1, created_at)
rcm_org_brief (ownership org; fields title, owner_id): fields title only
rcm_b (fields title, owner_id) WITHOUT sys_user registered: PERMISSION_DENIED 403
```

</details>
